data.title: Chat watcher: a loop stopped by the safety cap with work mid-lifecycle re-arms itself after a cooldown; maxLockWaitMs re-derived from the 60/75 tick box

data.body: BOARD DIRECTIVE (Claude Code chat, 2026-09-12: 'I did 4, want to do the rest?' — filed by the board's live session, item 2 of the 2026-09-11 inefficiency review). WHAT: (1) LOOP_DEFAULTS maxTicks (24) / maxMs (8 h) are runaway guards, not stop rules. When evaluate() returns cap-hit while any task is mid-lifecycle (MID_LIFECYCLE statuses) or a backlog task is ready, the watcher does not go idle: it records the cap in advance-loop.json (reason cap-hit, plus a rearmAt), waits a cooldown (default 10 min, env ADVANCE_LOOP_REARM_MIN), and starts a fresh loop armed by the same message id (a new startedAt and tick count — the cap still bounds each loop). Only nothing-actionable and no-progress end a loop for good; a new board message re-arms as today. WHY: the loop stopped on cap-hit at 11:21Z on 2026-09-12 with AS-71 and AS-113 in review and sat idle four hours until the board posted at 15:21Z; the same happened at 02:14Z the night before. (2) LOOP_DEFAULTS.maxLockWaitMs (60 min) was sized to exceed tick timeout (30) + staleness (45); both moved on 2026-09-11 (ADVANCE_TICK_TIMEOUT_MIN=60, ADVANCE_LOCK_STALE_MIN=75), so derive it from config (tickTimeoutMin + lockStaleMin, in ms) instead of a literal. ACCEPTANCE (M4): a fixture loop that hits maxTicks with a task in review must show a rearmAt in the state file and a LOOP-FIRE after the cooldown on injected clocks; the same fixture with an empty board must stop for good (the falsifier: delete the mid-lifecycle check and the second case re-arms — observed red). complexity: medium. Files: apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs (evaluate/settle/resume, LOOP_DEFAULTS), test/watcher-loop*.test.js, apps/chat/watch/README.md, the plist template comment.

Fold-in from AS-113's review (Ruben F1, 2026-09-12): the watcher multiplies ADVANCE_TICK_TIMEOUT_MIN / ADVANCE_LOCK_STALE_MIN / DEPLOY_TIMEOUT_MIN by 60000 straight into setTimeout, so any value above 35791 minutes crosses Node's 2^31-1 ms ceiling and fires after ~1 ms (reproduced: 35792 min SIGTERMs the tick after 2 ms). Operator-error only. Since this task re-derives maxLockWaitMs from the 60/75 tick box, its plan should refuse (not clamp) any minute value whose ms product exceeds 2147483647, the same shape AS-113 gave the chat probe budget, with one observed red per env var.

Planner breadcrumb (cto-owen, headless tick watcher:79108 loop 2 tick 2, on Opus under the Fable fallback). Plan at .lattice/plans/task_01M2B3P03HKQSD6QYKB4PTMSR7.md (66 lines), commit 155a717. DECIDED: (1) cap-hit with work remaining still goes through stop() — LOOP-STOP, lastLoop, loop=null stay the single exit — then the state machine enters a cooldown (rearm={at,armedBy}; mirror gains rearmAt, keeps armedBy); a new rearmIfDue() called once in poll() before nextPollAction builds a fresh loop (startedAt now, ticks 0, same armedBy) and the existing lock/deploy/LOOP-FIRE path does the rest. 'Work remains' is decided in the predicate as detail.rearm = mid-lifecycle or ready backlog — never a new message, since a message fire calls start(), which clears the cooldown. (2) The cooldown survives a watcher restart (resume() honours rearmAt) — the self-restart after THIS merge would otherwise drop it. (3) AS-129 subsumes AS-104: resume() checks capReached() before firing; work → cooldown, dry → stop cap-hit. Orchestrator cancels AS-104 at merge citing criteria 9a/9b. (4) loopLimits(config): maxLockWaitMs = (tickTimeoutMin + lockStaleMin) min → 135 min on the host; LOOP_DEFAULTS derives from DEFAULTS, no literal survives. DEFAULTS stay 30/45 — the plist is the 60/75 source. (5) envMinutes() THROWS (not clamps, not falls back) when v*60000 > 2147483647 for all five *_MIN knobs incl. DEPLOY_COOLDOWN; under launchd that is a crash loop with the reason in launchd.err.log, AS-88's precedent, README says so. LEFT OUT: sidebar label for the cooldown (deriveLoop is field-by-field so rearmAt is invisible; UX residual for the next lib/loop-status.js task); moving DEFAULTS to 60/75. COUNTS: host 624→643 (+19), compose 624→643 with --build; 17 mutants with exact red sets tabled in the plan. Baseline observed at plan time: node --test 624/622/0/2. Implementer developer-marcus (owns makeLoopOps from AS-95; Lena just closed AS-121). Reviewer qa-ruben (AS-104 and the fold-in are his findings — the review checks the work against them, and he is warm on the resume/lock seams). Branch feat/AS-129-loop-cap-rearm, worktree .worktrees/AS-129. Notes: scratchpad/agent-cto-owen/AS-129/planning-notes.md.

Implementation (developer-marcus, tick watcher:79108 loop 2 tick 3, on Opus). Branch feat/AS-129-loop-cap-rearm, tip a445e9c, 6 commits, tree clean.

Built, all in apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs: exported capReached/workRemains/loopLimits/MAX_TIMER_MS; cap-hit detail gains rearm; makeLoopOps has a private rearm state — settle() still stop()s on cap-hit then cooldown()s when detail.rearm, rearmIfDue() arms a fresh loop (ticks 0, new startedAt, same armedBy, pending), start() clears the cooldown, mirror() adds rearmAt and keeps armedBy while cooling, resume() evaluates the cap before owing a tick (AS-104) and re-enters a cooldown from an inactive mirror's rearmAt, snapshot() exposes rearmAt+limits. LOOP_DEFAULTS.maxLockWaitMs derived from DEFAULTS; rearmMs added. envMinutes() throws past 2147483647 ms for all five *_MIN knobs. Unguarded wiring (crit 11): poll() `loopOps.rearmIfDue();` before nextPollAction; start() `limits: loopLimits(config)`; loadConfig `loopRearmMin: envMinutes(...)`. README (file row, rule f, "After the cap", lock-wait, resume, ceiling, reading lines) and plist comment updated.

Tests: 19 new + T10 rewrite. Host 643/641/0/2 (from 624/622/0/2). Compose asc-impl-as129 --build 643/635/0/8, receipt "Image asc-impl-as129-test Built", down clean, 0 leaks.

Mutants: 17/17 killed, full suite per mutant, in place with restore and `git diff --exit-code` clean after each; hunks in the log. 15 exact as tabled. Two wider, both implied by the plan's own test specs: M1 {T3,T6,T9b,T12} (T9b's dry-board resume calls workRemains); M3 {T5,T8,T11} (T8 asserts rearmIfDue false at T0).

Deviations: T11/T12 limits add maxNoProgress:10 (headOf null in temp repo, no-progress precedes the cap); T6 uses maxTicks:1 (dry stops at tick 1 under a 2-tick cap); rearmIfDue has a defensive loop!==null branch; resume's cap stop detail adds resumed:true and mirrors; watcher-main harness accepts over.loopOps as a ctx function.

advance-loop.json sha256 unchanged (crit 12). No `60 * 60 * 1000` lock-wait literal remains (only maxMs and retention arithmetic). Nothing left undone. Residual as planned: sidebar "re-arming in N min" label.

Scratchpad: scratchpad/agent-developer-marcus/AS-129/ (progress.md, mutants.log, mutants.mjs, compose-run.log, hash files).
